text:
1. Safe passage. Bring your own luck.
2. Rest here. The dust does not sleep.
3. Well water. Mind the reflection.
4. Coyote watch. They know your pace.
5. Grave of a stranger. Do not borrow his fate.
6. Canyon rim. The view improves with breath.
7. Dead end. The road continues.
8. Snake pit. Dry heat.
9. Gang territory. Polite words are cheap.
10. Your soul. Keep it close.

1A. Set your pack on the step, where I can see your hands. I have kept this door since the oak was pale. Some folk I turn away come back with less to carry.
1B. You may knock once; I am old, not deaf. Before I lift the bar, tell me who knows you have come. There is a bench here for those who need time to answer.
2A. Mind the oil tin by your foot. I light these lamps from the gate to the tower, then walk back to see which have gone out. If you leave after dark, I will be on that round.
2B. Stand near the lamp while you look for your name on that list. They write the names small, and rain gets under the glass. I have asked for a roof over it, but they gave me a brighter wick.
3A. Keep to my left; the sword hangs on my right. I can hold this gate against six men, if the hinges hold. I used to know why six men would want it.
3B. You have come without a shield. There are spare ones in the guardroom, though you will have to scrape off the names. Mine belonged to a man who taught me what we were guarding, but he is dead, and no one gives the same answer now.
4A. Did you hear me on the road? When the sound stopped, did you stop too? What brought you the rest of the way?
4B. Can you see the rope beside the gate? Will you pull it once for the keeper, or twice for the dead? Have they left no way to ring for someone who is lost?
